entries.api: rclcppyy.enable_cpp_acceleration() before rclpy/message imports
entries.notes: Creates an accelerated node, redirects a flat message type, and completes a C++ pub/sub round trip in an isolated interpreter.

entries.api: RCLCPPYY_ENABLE_HOOK=1 with an installed startup hook
entries.notes: A fresh interpreter proves create_node and spin_once are patched when the opt-in variable is exactly 1.

entries.api: Installed startup hook with RCLCPPYY_ENABLE_HOOK unset or not 1
entries.notes: Fresh interpreters remain on unmodified stock behavior.

entries.api: enable_cpp_acceleration() after rclpy or message modules are imported
entries.notes: There is best-effort conversion of already imported names, but class aliases and node subclasses captured before patching do not yet have a differential contract test.

entries.api: rclpy.create_node()
entries.notes: Returns RclcppyyNode. The object currently contains both a Python node and a separate C++ node, so graph-identity certification remains separate.

entries.api: rclcppyy.Node(name)
entries.notes: Direct construction and get_name are tested; broader Node behavior is covered by individual entries.

entries.api: Node name/namespace and endpoint identity observed through the ROS graph
entries.notes: The internal C++ node currently uses a suffixed name and is distinct from the Python node; no transparent graph-identity guarantee exists.

entries.api: Existing subclasses of a Node alias imported before activation
entries.notes: Replacing rclpy.node.Node does not rewrite class objects or aliases captured before activation.

entries.api: Generated .msg class imported after activation
entries.notes: A flat generated message resolves to its C++ class, supports keyword construction, and traverses pub/sub without Python message conversion.

entries.api: Nested messages and primitive sequences on the unpatched-message native rclcpp path
entries.notes: The reusable native path has recursive conversion and sequence coverage; transparent import-hook identity for these shapes is not implied.

entries.api: Generated service and action class import redirection
entries.notes: The current import finder recognizes .msg._ modules only.

entries.api: Node.create_publisher(message_type, topic, depth_or_qos)
entries.notes: Default publisher creation and ordered payload delivery are covered for flat, nested, and primitive-sequence examples.

entries.api: Publisher callback_group, event_callbacks, qos_overriding_options, and publisher_class
entries.notes: Several options are currently accepted but ignored rather than preserving the requested behavior.

entries.api: Node.create_subscription(message_type, topic, callback, depth_or_qos)
entries.notes: Default subscription creation, C++ message callback delivery, and ordered payloads are covered.

entries.api: Subscription callback_group, event_callbacks, qos_overriding_options, raw mode, and content filters
entries.notes: Requested callback groups, events, overrides, and raw delivery are ignored or not represented.

entries.api: Node.create_timer(period, Python callback)
entries.notes: The benchmark exercises the path, but one-shot behavior, callback groups, cancellation/reset, exception propagation, and destruction lack contract tests.

entries.api: rclpy.spin(accelerated_node)
entries.notes: Delegates to rclcpp::spin, but callback exceptions, shutdown, and mixed entities are not contract-certified.

entries.api: rclpy.spin_once(accelerated_node, timeout_sec=...)
entries.notes: The hook and ROS CLI scenario cover the patched path; exact callback-count, timeout, and executor-argument semantics remain unverified.

entries.api: Custom executors, MultiThreadedExecutor, callback groups, and waitables
entries.notes: The compatibility product currently targets its own single-threaded rclcpp spin path.

entries.api: Node.create_service/create_client and service spinning
entries.notes: Inherited Python entities are not serviced by the patched rclcpp spin path.

entries.api: rclpy.action ActionClient and ActionServer
entries.notes: No compatibility adapter or safe mixed-executor fallback is present.

entries.api: Local parameters, parameter services, and parameter events
entries.notes: The Python base node owns parameters, while the accelerated spin path services the separate C++ node. Transparent local/remote behavior is not certified.

entries.api: rclpy.lifecycle.LifecycleNode
entries.notes: Lifecycle node construction and transition services are not patched.

entries.api: Normal interpreter exit after rclcpp bringup and node creation
entries.notes: An isolated process returns normally without a forced exit or teardown fault.

entries.api: Repeated init/shutdown cycles and multiple contexts
entries.notes: No differential lifecycle matrix currently proves this behavior.

entries.api: C++ message CDR serialization compared with rclpy.serialization
entries.notes: Flat and tested message bytes match the stock serializer; this is a native capability and not yet a global rclpy.serialization patch.
